caption: The stokvel is the one thing we've never skipped, even the tight months. What's yours?

slides.title:
How we spend
our R33 000
household income
Living in Zeerust
slides.body:
Him 35, her 32
Married, two kids (9 and 6)
Jobs: Farm equipment mechanic & Grade R classroom assistant
Combined net: R33 000 p/m

slides.title: Bond
slides.includes: 3 bed on the edge of town, borehole water
slides.body: We bought here because the schools are close enough to walk. The borehole was a bonus we didn't plan for.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Two adults, two growing boys, a bulk shop once a month
slides.body: Feeding two boys under ten costs more than either of us budgeted for two years ago.

slides.title: Car instalment
slides.includes: His single cab, used for farm call-outs
slides.body: One vehicle between us. It's tight, but a second instalment would be worse.

slides.title: School fees & uniforms
slides.includes: Two kids, fees, stationery, growing out of shoes
slides.body: Every January this number surprises us like it hasn't happened six times before.

slides.title: Stokvel contribution
slides.includes: A twelve-woman stokvel, payout due in December
slides.body: It's the one saving we've never once skipped, even in months this tight.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Fuel, medical aid, borehole pump maintenance, phone & fibre, funeral policies, insurance, kids' extra-murals
slides.body: None of these feel optional and none of them are small once you add them up.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R33 000, for a family of four. It goes further here than it would in Johannesburg, but not by much.

slides.title: We stopped guessing
slides.body:
We uploaded our statements to Beyond Horizon and it sorted every transaction into categories for us.

Seeing school costs and the farm fuel bill side by side changed how we plan for January.

No bank login needed.
